airport.name: Milford Municipal-Ben and Judy Briscoe Field

summary: Milford Municipal-Ben and Judy Briscoe Field is a small general aviation airport serving the rural community of Milford in southwestern Utah. The facility was renamed to honor Ben and Judy Briscoe, long-time supporters of the airport and local aviation. It provides convenient access to the Beaver County region and serves as a useful gateway for visitors exploring Utah's remote desert landscapes and outdoor recreation opportunities.
faqs:
Q: What is the airport code for Milford Municipal Airport?
A: The IATA code is MLF and the ICAO code is KMLF.

Q: What type of airport is Milford Municipal?
A: It is a small public-use airport primarily serving general aviation traffic.

Q: Does Milford Municipal offer commercial flights?
A: No, the airport does not offer scheduled commercial service; it mainly supports private and recreational flying.

Q: Who are the Briscoes the airport is named after?
A: The airport honors Ben and Judy Briscoe, recognized for their contributions to the local aviation community.
transport_tips: The airport is located just outside the small town of Milford, with only a short drive needed to reach local accommodations and services. Rental cars are not typically available on-site, so arranging ground transportation in advance is recommended. The nearest larger airports with commercial service are located in Cedar City and Salt Lake City.
local_tip: Fuel up before arriving—Milford is a remote desert community with limited services, so plan your stops carefully when flying in for backcountry adventures or visits to nearby public lands.
